subject: Aurora Labs — tri-region activation runbook request
messages:
From: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@auroralabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Labs Ops <ops@auroralabs.com>, procure@auroralabs.com
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Regional capacity ask — Aurora workload forecast attached

Hi Hannah,

We're ramping the Aurora product rollout across APAC, EU, and US and need Redwood to propose a tri-region dedicated deployment plan tied to our upcoming purchase order (deal DL-2027-049). Attached is our Q2–Q4 traffic forecast (CSV) and a short note on expected model mix. High level:

- Region priority: Sydney (APAC pilot) first, Dublin (EU) second, us-west (primary US) third.
- Peak concurrent requests (tokens-in-flight): APAC 550 concurrent, EU 420, US 760.
- Typical model mix: 60% mid-sized generation (approx ~2k token context), 25% embeddings, 15% heavy LLMs for longer context traces.
- SLOs: 95th latency target ~200–250ms for generation calls; embedding throughput is higher priority during batch windows.
- Data residency: APAC traffic must remain in APAC region.

Can your team propose an activation runbook (pre-warm, burst lanes, failover) and preliminary GPU counts/SKUs so we can align PO timelines? We also need a stub SOW to share with procurement.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Zhang
Head of Platform — Aurora Labs

Attachment: aurora_traffic_forecast_Q2-Q4.csv

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@auroralabs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional capacity ask — Aurora workload forecast attached

Thanks Claire — got the forecast. A few clarifying questions before we finalize sizing:

1) Peak concurrency definition: is the APAC 550 figure steady-state peak (sustained for >30m) or a short burst (sub-5m)?
2) Model families: can you share the top two model checkpoints you're planning to serve (we need to know memory footprints for KV cache planning)?
3) Retention/Logging: any special audit log retention beyond our default 30 days?
4) Ramp expectations: is the Sydney pilot a hard date (must be live by X) or soft?

Prelim idea — we can draft a runbook that stages activation: pre-warm 30% of nodes for pilot, enable burst lanes for 2x short bursts, and a 20% failover cushion per region. I'll loop in David and Karthik for a quick first-pass sizing + SOW stub. Would 30 minutes tomorrow for a quick triage call work?

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

On 2027-04-04 09:12, Claire Zhang wrote:
> We're ramping the Aurora product rollout across APAC, EU, and US and need Redwood to propose a tri-region dedicated deployment plan...

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Claire Zhang <c.zhang@auroralabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional capacity ask — Aurora workload forecast attached

Claire / team — reviewed the CSV quickly and sketched a conservative first-pass sizing (attached XLSX):

Summary (first-pass, pre-warm 30% baseline, 20% failover reserve):
- Sydney (ap-southeast-2): 8 x H100 (for low-latency heavy LLMs) + 6 x A100 80GB for sustained generation and embeddings. Pre-warm 4 H100-equivalent nodes to hit 30% baseline; reserve 2 nodes as burst buffer.
- Dublin (eu-west-1): 6 x A100 80GB + 2 x T4-class edge nodes for embedding batch windows; pre-warm 2 A100.
- us-west (us-west-2): 10 x A100 80GB (primary US footprint), with 3 x H100 for complex long-context inference.

Operational notes:
- Batching and KV prefix caching expected to reduce token cost ~18–25% depending on request pattern; our sizing assumes moderate caching (50% hit rate).
- Node startup time (cold): 6–8 minutes for A100 images, 10–12 minutes for H100 unless pre-warmed. Pre-warm nodes for the pilot critical to meet 95th latency SLO.
- Autoscaler settings: 2–3 second decision window for small ramps; use a 60s smoothing window to avoid thrash.
- Suggested quantization profiles for embeddings-heavy workloads to reduce memory pressure for Dublin.

Attached: proposed_node_layout_v2.xlsx (spread shows per-model throughput assumptions and headroom).

If this looks directionally correct, we can refine with Aurora's exact model checkpoints and provide costed SOW.

— David
David Kim
Senior Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_node_layout_v2.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Claire Zhang <c.zhang@auroralabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional capacity ask — Aurora workload forecast attached

Thanks David — that first-pass looks reasonable. A couple of commercial / prioritization points to align on:

- Order of activation: Aurora asked Sydney first. Given lead times and node availability, we should commit to a staged activation: phase 1 (pre-warm 30% in Sydney) -> phase 2 (scale to 60% after 2 weeks) -> phase 3 (full scale by day 90 or tied to usage triggers).
- Commitments & discounts: recommend the commercial team propose a 6–9 month committed tranche for Sydney to cover pre-warm and reserved capacity; this reduces unit costs and gives Aurora predictable latency.
- Cost vs speed trade: H100-heavy footprint increases capex by ~18% but reduces 95th latency and greatly helps long-context work. Propose mixed SKU approach described by David.

Laura — can you run a quick committed vs on-demand cost delta for this configuration and draft a minimal SOW timeline? Claire — is Aurora open to a pilot PO (smaller dollar amount) for the pre-warm phase?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@auroralabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional capacity ask — Aurora workload forecast attached

Claire — looping in procurement & sending a stub SOW (attached PDF). Quick notes from finance / SOW ops: 

- Estimated monthly run-rate (committed tranche) for phase 1 (Sydney pre-warm 30%, staged scale): $145,000/month (includes 10% margin buffer).
- Full steady-state (all three regions at suggested sizing): ~$375,000/month committed. On-demand delta is approximately +28% at current market rates.
- Proposed timeline: Finalize SOW and SKUs by 2027-04-09, pilot pre-warm turned on within 5 business days of signed pilot PO, then 3-week ramp to phase 2.
- Attachments: sow_stub_Aurora_Sydney.pdf (status: draft).

Next steps:
1) Aurora to confirm acceptance of staging plan (pilot PO for pre-warm) or request alternate commercial terms.
2) Aurora to share exact model checkpoints and any compliance requirements for APAC data residency.
3) Redwood infra (David) to finalize node images and pre-warm schedule once PO is received.

I'll prepare a short cost appendix and a DL for procurement to sign off. Claire — can you confirm whether procurement prefers a single global SOW or regionally scoped SOWs?

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sow_stub_Aurora_Sydney.pdf
